rules.rule: Never suggest lowering a CI threshold, deleting/skipping/weakening a test, relaxing an assertion, bypassing type checks, disabling a security/policy/audit check, or reducing coverage/mutation/audit requirements — unless the same PR replaces it with a stronger equivalent.

This repo is the canonical contracts kernel: types, JSON Schemas, Zod validators, and state machines ONLY. Flag any code that adds runtime execution, orchestration, agents, judges/LLM-judge logic, deterministic gate/harness logic, job queues, schedulers, provider/LLM adapters, optimization/RL engines, or runtime telemetry emission. The kernel defines OTel/Evidence-Bundle SHAPES; it must never run them. New top-level dirs like services/, workers/, runtime/, orchestrator/, or new src/ subpaths like src/runtime/, src/judges/, src/adapters/, src/server/, src/db/ are out of role (FORBIDDEN.md Axis 2/3). If a change feels like runtime, it belongs in a sibling repo (audit-harness / j-rig / intent-rollout-gate), not here.

The kernel makes no network calls, persists nothing, and runs no servers. Flag any new package.json runtime dependency that is an HTTP client (axios/got/undici/node-fetch), web framework (express/fastify/hono/next), DB driver or ORM (pg/mysql/mongodb/prisma/drizzle), job queue (bullmq/bull/@temporalio), LLM provider SDK (openai/@anthropic-ai/cohere-ai/groq-sdk), observability runtime (@opentelemetry/sdk-node, dd-trace, prom-client), storage SDK (@aws-sdk/*, @google-cloud/storage), or auth/session lib (jsonwebtoken/jose/passport). Runtime deps are hard-capped at 8 and must be listed in ALLOWLIST.md with a Blueprint-tied rationale (FORBIDDEN.md Axis 1 + ALLOWLIST.md).

Predicate URIs, in-toto predicate identifiers, OTel attribute namespaces, and attestation predicate hosts MUST live at evals.intentsolutions.io and MUST NEVER use labs.intentsolutions.io as a live host. This is a CISO binding (DR-004 + DR-010 section 10) with NO override path. Flag any schema $id, predicate constant, URL literal, or fixture that uses labs.intentsolutions.io as a predicate/attestation/namespace host. (Lines that merely document the prohibition are fine.)

The kernel IS the single source of truth for the 14 canonical entities (Blueprint B's 13 + SkillVersion) and the gate-result/v1 predicate. Peer repos (audit-harness, j-rig, intent-rollout-gate) import these contracts; they never redefine them. Flag any change that locally re-declares a canonical entity type, copies a kernel JSON Schema instead of referencing it, or forks the gate-result/v1 shape. Within this repo, flag duplicate/divergent definitions of the same entity across src/entities, schemas, and validators that would let the three representations drift.

Per the DR-010 unification thesis, every new canonical contract must ship as a coherent triplet: the JSON Schema (schemas/v1/*.schema.json, draft 2020-12), the Zod validator (src/validators/v1/), and the entity type + state machine (src/entities/, src/state-machines/) — kept in lockstep and Evidence-Bundle-compatible. Flag a new entity type added without its schema + validator, a schema added without a matching validator, or a state machine whose transition map diverges from the entity it governs. The schema, the Zod validator, and the TS type must describe the same shape.

The TypeScript strictness floor is non-negotiable and may only ratchet UP. Flag any change that loosens strict mode or removes a strict flag (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride, noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature, verbatimModuleSyntax) in tsconfig*.json, introduces `any` (explicit or via eslint-disable of no-explicit-any), uses a non-type import for a type-only symbol (consistent-type-imports), or drops the .js extension on a relative import under NodeNext. Loosening the floor requires an explicit ADR, never an inline edit.

src/index.ts re-exports only stable, promoted contracts. Flag changes that re-export work-in-progress / internal types from the public barrel before they are promoted, or that export a runtime-tier symbol from an authoring-tier path (and vice versa). Validators are an opt-in subpath (@intentsolutions/core/validators/v1) so types-only consumers pay zero zod cost — flag changes that pull zod into the main types entry.
